acceptanceCriteria: With a declared progress signal, a hand-off whose fingerprint changed is not a no-progress generation for loop detection, backoff or NO_PROGRESS_HANDOFF.
A hand-off with an unchanged fingerprint and no candidate, gate or review still counts as no progress.
Without the declaration, behaviour is unchanged.
Findings and holds name the signal that judged them.
The declared signal is recorded as loop evidence, so the decision can be audited.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1050 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Loop detection (`loopDetection`, CAL-V0-102), the dispatcher's no-progress backoff, and the doctor kinds NO_PROGRESS_HANDOFF, REPEAT_REFUSAL and SETUP_ONLY_PROOF all judge progress by queue artefacts: a new candidate tree, a gate result, or a review. Many adopters make real progress between hand-offs without producing any of those mid-work. They commit to a working branch, record witnessed obligations, or advance a run plan, and submit a candidate only at the end. For such a program: - NO_PROGRESS_HANDOFF fires on nearly every active ticket. One ticket showed 31 consecutive hand-offs while it was steadily progressing. - Enabling `loopDetection` would hold almost every ticket LOOP_DETECTED, each needing an owner `ticket reopen`, and the opt-in cannot be undone on that store. The adopter therefore keeps its own stall rule and its own doctor detectors, which duplicates these feature See beamfall/corvint#1050 for the full text.
title: Loop detection, backoff and no-progress doctor kinds: accept an adopter-declared progress signal (issue #1050)
